Kenya_2026-06-15_weekly_precip: ECMWF S2S ensemble-mean rainfall for 15 to 22 June is concentrated on the coast and across the Somali border, with 35 to 45 mm near the north coast around 3S and 12 to 18 mm along the eastern border, while most of the interior stays below 5 mm. From 22 June to 27 July the coast eases to 15 to 30 mm per week and the west along the Uganda border receives 15 to 25 mm, peaking near 2N. The northern and central interior remain almost dry (below 3 mm) in every week.
Kenya_2026-06-15_weekly_precip_downscale: Downscaled ECMWF rainfall for 15 to 22 June exceeds 60 mm on the north coast and its hinterland around 1S to 2.5S, with 15 to 30 mm along the rest of the coast and only 10 to 20 mm in the west. From 22 June to 13 July the coastal strip holds 30 to 55 mm, with the maximum moving to the south coast in the week of 29 June to 6 July, and the western highlands near the equator pick up 30 to 50 mm. From 13 to 27 July the main maximum is in the west (40 to 55 mm around 35E), and the northern and eastern interior stay dry throughout.
Kenya_2026-06-15_weekly_medium_range_pre: The medium-range ECMWF forecast for 15 to 22 June puts 30 to 55 mm along the coast, heaviest on the south coast and just offshore south of 4S, and 25 to 35 mm across the Somali border east of 41E, with the interior below 5 mm. For 22 to 29 June the coast eases to 10 to 18 mm and the rain shifts to the west, with 20 to 35 mm and isolated cells near 60 mm along the Uganda border and the western highlands between 2N and 1S. Totals of 40 to 60 mm lie north of 6N in southern Ethiopia in the second week.
Kenya_2026-06-15_chance_of_above_or_belo: The tercile balance for 15 to 22 June shows a very strong split, with a below-normal lean of -75 to -100 points across the whole west, northwest and centre and an above-normal lean of +75 to +100 points from the Somali border to the coast. From 22 June to 27 July the below-normal lean of -50 to -100 points persists over the north-centre and northwest, while the east and the coast stay at +40 to +75 points. The southwest turns neutral to slightly above normal (+25 to +50 points) from 29 June onward.
Kenya_2026-06-15_efi_sot_precip: A wet extreme is signalled for 15 to 22 June along the Somali border and the far east between the equator and 4N, where the EFI is 0.65 to 0.85, and on the north coast near 1.5S to 3.5S (0.65 to 0.75), both enclosed by a SOT zero contour. No part of Kenya has an EFI above 0.5 in any later week through 27 July. The only other feature is a small SOT contour in central Kenya on the equator for 13 to 20 July without EFI shading.
Kenya_2026-06-15_50th_percentile_exedanc: The chance of exceeding the model-climate median for 15 to 22 June is below 1% over most of the west, northwest and centre, against 90 to 100% along the eastern border and the coast. From 22 June to 27 July the north-centre stays at 1 to 10% and the west at 10 to 45%, while the east holds 55 to 90% with cells of 90 to 99% on the Somali border near the equator between 29 June and 13 July. The south rises to 55 to 90% from 29 June.
Kenya_2026-06-15_anomaly_from_50th: The ensemble mean for 15 to 22 June is 25 to 31 mm above the model-climate median on the north coast and the adjacent Somali border and 10 to 15 mm above it along the eastern border up to 3N, against deficits of 15 to 25 mm in the west and northwest along the Uganda border. From 22 June to 27 July the western deficits ease to 5 to 15 mm, largest near Lake Victoria on the equator, and the coastal surplus settles at 8 to 15 mm near 3S. The centre and south stay close to the median.
Kenya_2026-04-20_weekly_precip: ECMWF S2S ensemble-mean rainfall for 20 to 27 April is 30 to 45 mm across the north and west, 60 to 75 mm at the western edge of the domain over Lake Victoria, and 60 to 90 mm on the south coast and offshore south of 3S. The week of 27 April to 4 May is the wettest, with 55 to 70 mm over the western half between 2N and 2S and the central highlands, 90 to 115 mm over Lake Victoria and 40 to 60 mm on the coast. Totals then decline countrywide, with the north and east below 15 mm by 18 May and only 20 to 30 mm left in the west and on the coast by 25 May to 1 June.
Kenya_2026-04-20_efi_sot_precip: No wet-extreme signal is present for 20 to 27 April. For 27 April to 4 May the EFI reaches 0.6 to 0.7 over Lake Victoria at the western edge of the domain between 0.5N and 2S, with a SOT zero contour, and about 0.6 in one cell in central Kenya on the equator. No EFI shading above 0.5 appears from 4 May to 1 June, apart from a very small SOT contour in central Kenya for 4 to 11 May.
